title: How To Have Classroom Management Presence https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2013/03/30/how-to-have-classroom-management-presence/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes 'presence'—an intangible quality that causes students to naturally behave well—as arising not from a teacher's appearance or mannerisms but from an internal belief system. He breaks presence into two seemingly opposite attitudes: caring deeply enough about students to only use long-term, proven classroom management principles, combined with an emotional refusal to let misbehavior personally affect the teacher's mood or enjoyment. He explains that this combination lets teachers abandon reactive tactics like yelling, scolding, bribery, and false praise in favor of consistently following a classroom management plan, which shifts the balance of power in the relationship. The result, he argues, is a durable, intrinsic form of student motivation rather than the weak, temporary compliance produced by emotional reactivity.
points: Classroom management 'presence' comes from an internal belief system, not from appearance, dress, or mannerisms.
The first attitude required is caring deeply enough about students to rely only on long-term, proven classroom management principles rather than short-term reactive tactics.
The second, harder attitude is refusing to let student misbehavior affect the teacher's mood or enjoyment—'you mustn't care if they misbehave.'
Presence requires abandoning false praise, yelling, scolding, lecturing, bribery, and other reactive or manipulative methods.
The combination of deep care with emotional non-reactivity shifts the balance of power in the relationship and produces durable, intrinsic student motivation.
quotes: There exists a cadre of teachers who are able to command effortless respect and polite behavior from their students.
Rather, it comes from a deep-seated belief they carry with them on the inside, which gives them a level of confidence, calmness, and freedom that eludes most of their colleagues.
It is this: From the moment your students arrive in the morning until they leave for the day, you mustn’t care if they misbehave.
Thus, you must no longer rely on false praise, yelling, scolding, lecturing, questioning, glaring, pleading, eye-rolling, bribery, intimidation, or any other temporary or reactionary method.
To care without caring will fill you with a gentle but strong leadership presence your students will respect and love you for.
This rare combination of deep care with seemingly no care at all will transform your class from one that is extrinsically motivated to behave... to one that is intrinsically motivated.
